governance.parent: City of Warsaw and the Minister of Culture and National Heritage

basis: The house is a branch of the Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw (statute article 9), whose statute annexed to the 2 January 2025 agreement gives the City supervision (article 10), and whose 2025 financial statement page 2 names the form as a municipal cultural institution with legal personality.

controls: approval of programme, loans or disposals by a ministry or council

basis: The consolidated founding decision of the Museum and Galleries of Ljubljana, as amended to 2022, gives the form (articles 1 and 3, a public institution founded by the City), the director (the City Council appoints, article 26), the board's consent to the financial plan (article 19), the Plečnik House among the City property it manages (article 36) and the City's prior consent to contracts on that property (article 24).

The foundation's statutes give a non-profit foundation with its own legal personality formed from a savings bank (articles 1 and 4), the board's budget approval and the Generalitat's control through the foundations protectorate (article 4 and the board's reserved powers), and the board's power to name the director general (article 33).

governance.parent: Barcelona City Council, through the Institut de Cultura de Barcelona (ICUB)

basis: The museum's own who-we-are page says it belongs to Barcelona City Council as part of the Institut de Cultura.

The foundation's mission page calls it a public non-profit foundation created in 2006 from the cession of the house to the Ajuntament, and its statutes of 20 June 2022 give the mayor as president (article 10), the board's budget approval (article 14 list of reserved powers) and the Protectorat's role.

FUNDOS's statutes give an ordinary non-profit foundation formed from a savings bank (article 1), the Patronato's power to approve the budget and name the director (articles 16 and 27) and the Protectorado's role, and its transparency page states the founding.

The 2026 director selection brief page 1 calls the foundation a private non-profit entity run by a board, says the board approves the budget and, on page 4, votes the final appointment of the director.
